.ER'OR BIVAHENO PINOY Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMEÉ€ A. Francisco Gold Condominium II EDSA Cor. Mapagmahal St., Diliman Quezon City LEGAL SERVICE Legal Opinion No. 37 s. 2011 JUL 08 2011 HON. NINO A. TAYCO HON. WILLIAM T. BIHAG HON. ANGELO N. REMO HON. ROBERT B. BRAZOS HON. JEFF LINDSAY C. LEE OLIVER Sangguniang Bayan Members Pasacao, Camarines Sur Distinguished SB Members, This has reference to your letter dated 22 June 2011 seeking this Department's clarification on the application and legal effect of DILG Legal Opinion No. 19, S. 2011. Your letter pointed out several pieces of information allegedly omitted by Pasacao Mayor Asuncion Villamante-Arceno (Mayor Arceno) in her request for legal opinion with this Department relative to the enforcement of Ordinance No. 01 S. 201 1 enacted by the Sangguniang Bayan of Pasacao. Among the averments in your letter, the most notable information which you furnished this Department is the fact that you have already filed Special Civil Action No. 2011-0035 with the Regional Trial Court, 5th Judicial Region of Naga City, with the caption "Petition to Declare Appropriation Ordinance No. 01 S. 2011 of the Municipality of Pasacao Illegal and Void ab initio with Prayer for the Issuance of TRO, Writ of Preliminary Injunction and Writ of Permanent Injunction." The application for the provisional remedy of preliminary injunction had already been granted by the RTC in its Order dated 29 March 201 1 wherein the respondents therein, including Mayor Arceno were enjoined by the court from doing any act or deed that would lead or result to the disbursement and disposition of public funds pursuant to Appropriation Ordinance No. 01 S. 2011 of the Municipality of Pasacao, or from doing any act that would lead to its implementation during the pendency of the case. Therefore, when Mayor Arceno submitted her request for legal opinion with this Department on 23 May 2011, the court order was already in effect. However, it should be made clear that the pendency of the case and the court order dated 29 March 201 1 were not mentioned in Mayor Arceno's request for legal opinion.

At this instant, it is worthy to note that the principles laid down in Legal Opinions issued by this Department are mainly based on the factual allegations contained in the communications sent by the requester/s and the attachments included thereto. Hence, a Legal Opinion must be taken as it is written, i.e., an interpretation of the provisions of the Local Government Code of 1991 as applied to a given set of facts made available to the Department. Coming now to your instant request, please be advised that DILG Legal Opinion No. 19 S. 2011 was not issued with the view of defying the court order for preliminary injunction, since this Department was not properly informed of the same. In this connection, please be informed that in deference to the jurisdiction of the courts, this Department had already issued Memorandum Order No. 2()10-02 dated 17 September 2010 which provides for the guidelines on requests for legal opinions submitted to this Department. Item number three (3) of the memorandum states that this Department shall not act on queries that are litis pendencia, or pending litigation, except when the court itself requests for the opinion. Furthermore, it provides that in the event that an opinion has been rendered by the Department and its field officers without knowledge or infornnation that a case involving the issues raised in the query is pending in court, such opinion shall automatically be deemed ineffective. A copy of said memorandum is hereto attached for your reference. Perforce, DILG Opinion No. 19 S. 2011 is deemed ineffective, as the matters considered therein are litis pendencia. We hope to have clarified you on the matter. A LS:03 64 Very truly yours, Y. JES B. QUE Director 111
